sequences.description: SAML connector with CA validation; two similar identities authenticate via SP-initiated flow and verify identity + access.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage: SAML SP-initiated login for two identities with similar names; verify userinfo and protected read behavior.

sequences.description: SAML connector config change (toggle insecure signature validation) with re-authentication and verification before/after.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage: reconfigure SAML connector and re-authenticate; compare userinfo/read behavior across config versions.

sequences.description: Password grant login for two identities, session revocation, and post-revocation verification coverage.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage: exercise /token password grant, /userinfo, /token/revoke, and verify behavior for two users.

sequences.description: Create a SAML connector that maps groups and enforces allowedGroups with filterGroups=true; run SP-initiated SAML logins for two different identities and verify resulting identity metadata and access behavior.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage: SAML connector group mapping + allowedGroups gating + filterGroups claim filtering across two identities.

sequences.description: Register two OIDC clients with different redirect URIs, then run SP-initiated SAML logins through each client and verify identity and access for two identities.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage: create_application + start_oidc_auth variations (client/redirect) + SAML brokered login + verify identity/access across two identities.

sequences.description: Exercise a config change by deleting and recreating the SAML connector with a different entity_issuer, then re-authenticate and verify identity/access before and after.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage: cleanup_auth_method + enable_auth_method (recreate) + SP-initiated SAML login + verify identity/access across a connector config change.

sequences.description: Coverage: SP-initiated SAML flow with OneTimeUse + fixed Assertion ID reuse across two logins (replay-style coverage) for two identities; verify identity and protected read behavior after each login.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage-only: exercise SAML login variations (OneTimeUse, fixed assertion ID reuse) and verify endpoints across two identities.

sequences.description: Coverage: SAML connector with issuer pinned; perform a normal SAML login, then delete and recreate connector with different group delimiter and group filtering settings, then re-authenticate as a second identity and verify both sessions.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage-only: exercise connector delete/recreate config change and re-authentication; verify identity and read behavior across two identities.

sequences.description: Coverage: create an additional OIDC client, run SP-initiated SAML logins through two different clients for two identities, verify identity/read, then revoke one session and verify again.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage-only: exercise create_application, multi-client auth initiation, session revocation, and verify endpoints across two identities.

sequences.description: Coverage: create SAML connector with custom attribute mappings and group delimiter; run two SP-initiated auth requests with different scopes and realms for two distinct identities; verify identity and protected read for both sessions.

Create SAML connector with explicit grant/response types and custom NameID policy format; run two SP-initiated auth requests with different approval_prompt values and authenticate two distinct identities; verify identity and protected read for both sessions.
Create a new OIDC client and a SAML connector; run SP-initiated SAML login, revoke the session, then re-authenticate as a second identity and verify both sessions (pre/post revoke).

SAML connector lifecycle coverage: authenticate one identity, delete connector, recreate with different attribute mappings and group delimiter, then authenticate a second identity; verify identity and protected read for both sessions.
Coverage: create SAML connector with insecure signature validation enabled; run two SP-initiated SAML logins for two similar identities and verify identity + read behavior for both sessions.
Coverage: enable password connector + password grant, perform password login and SAML login, then revoke one session and verify both sessions again.

Coverage: SAML connector with strict group gating (allowedGroups) and filterGroups=false; authenticate two identities with different realms, then change connector to filterGroups=true and re-authenticate one identity to observe claim filtering differences.

Coverage: create a second SAML connector with different issuer/audience settings; run SP-initiated auth through each connector for two identities and verify identity + read behavior for both sessions.

sequences.description: Coverage: create an additional OIDC client and a SAML connector with explicit grant/response types; run two SP-initiated SAML logins for two identities using different clients and scopes; verify identity and read behavior for both sessions.

Coverage: create a new OIDC client plus a SAML connector pinned to explicit issuer/audience; run two SP-initiated auth requests with different state/nonce and scopes for two similar identities; exchange code for tokens and verify identity + read behavior for both sessions.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: coverage: exercise client creation + SAML connector creation with issuer/audience pinning, then two distinct SP-initiated SAML logins with different scopes/state/nonce and full verification.

sequences.description: SP-initiated SAML login for two similar identities, revoke one session, then re-authenticate the revoked identity and verify both sessions before/after.
Enable password connector for direct password login, then perform a SAML SP-initiated login for a second identity; verify identity and read behavior for both sessions.
Create SAML connector with pinned issuer/audience, authenticate one identity, then update connector issuer/audience settings and re-authenticate a second identity; verify both sessions.

Create a SAML connector with explicit NameID policy format and group attribute mapping; run SP-initiated SAML logins for two identities with similar emails but different NameIDs; verify identity and read behavior for both sessions.

Create an additional OIDC client and a SAML connector; run SP-initiated SAML login, exchange code for tokens, verify identity/read; then create a second client and repeat for a second identity to compare behavior across clients.

Enable a SAML connector, perform SP-initiated SAML login for one identity, revoke the resulting session, then re-login as a second identity and verify both sessions' identity/read behavior before and after revocation.

Create a new public OIDC client and a SAML connector; run SP-initiated SAML login for one identity and exchange code for tokens; then re-authenticate a second identity using the same connector but different scopes and exchange code; verify identity and read behavior for both sessions.

Enable password connector and perform a password login for one identity; then create a separate SAML connector and perform SP-initiated SAML login for a second identity; revoke the password session and verify both sessions before/after revocation.

Coverage: configure an OIDC upstream connector (for token_exchange coverage) and a SAML connector (for SP-initiated SAML coverage). Perform password login (if enabled) and token exchange against OIDC, then perform SP-initiated SAML login for a second identity and verify identity/read for both sessions.

Coverage: two separate SAML connectors (one strict, one insecure-skip-signature-validation) and two identities authenticate through different connectors; verify identity and read behavior for both sessions.
Coverage: create a new OIDC client, run SP-initiated SAML login for two identities, exchange code for tokens for each, verify identity/read, then revoke one session and verify both sessions again.

Coverage: password connector enabled, attempt two password logins for similar usernames, verify identity/read for both; then perform SP-initiated SAML login for one of them via a SAML connector and verify again to compare sessions.
Create a SAML connector with pinned issuer and explicit entityIssuer; run two SP-initiated SAML logins with different scopes; verify identity and read behavior for both sessions.
Create a password connector and perform two password logins; then revoke one session and verify both sessions again to observe revocation effects.

Create a new OIDC client, then create a SAML connector; run SP-initiated SAML login for one identity and exchange code for tokens; change client configuration by creating a second client and re-authenticate a second identity; verify identity/read for both sessions.

Create a SAML connector, run two SP-initiated SAML logins for two similar identities, verify both sessions, then delete the connector (config change) and attempt a third login to observe behavior post-cleanup; verify prior sessions again.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage: SAML connector lifecycle (create -> login -> cleanup) and session behavior across config change; multiple identities with similar names.

sequences.description: Enable password connector, perform two password logins for two identities, verify both, then create a SAML connector and perform SP-initiated SAML login for a third identity; revoke the SAML session and verify before/after revocation.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage: password grant + SAML browser flow in one run; session revocation effects on a SAML-derived session; multiple identities.

sequences.description: Create a new confidential OIDC client, run two OIDC authorization code flows (no upstream connector specified) for two identities, exchange codes for tokens, then verify identity and read behavior for both sessions.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: Coverage: client creation + OIDC auth code + token exchange + verification for two identities with different scopes.

sequences.description: Coverage: create two SAML connectors with different group handling (allowedGroups+filterGroups vs no allowedGroups). Run SP-initiated auth then SAML login for two identities across connectors, verify identity and read-secret for both sessions, then revoke one session and verify both again.

Create a SAML connector with group attributes and allowedGroups gating; run SP-initiated SAML logins for two identities (one intended to pass, one intended to fail) and verify identity/read outcomes for both sessions.

Create two OIDC clients (public vs confidential) and run SP-initiated SAML logins for two identities using different clients/scopes; exchange codes for tokens and verify identity/read for both sessions.

Config change + re-auth: create a SAML connector, authenticate one identity, then delete the connector and recreate it with different attribute mappings; re-authenticate a second identity and verify both sessions.
OIDC auth initiation with varying connector selection and approval prompt; then SAML callback attempts for two identities; verify identity and read behavior for both sessions.
SAML connector config change (cleanup + re-enable) between two SAML logins; verify both sessions and attempt a post-change login; includes session revocation and re-verification.
Mixed flows: password grant attempts for two similar usernames plus an OIDC auth initiation; verify identity/read for both password sessions and observe differences in metadata/policies.

Create a SAML connector with issuer/audience pinned, run two SP-initiated SAML logins with different scopes, verify identity and read-secret for both sessions, then revoke one session and verify both again.

Enable password connector and attempt two password logins with different scopes, verify both sessions, then perform a SAML login and finally cleanup the SAML connector and re-verify existing sessions.

Coverage sequence exercising SP-initiated SAML flow context, multiple SAML assertion variants (baseline, remove Conditions, include OneTimeUse, fixed Assertion ID reuse), and multi-identity logins with full verify coverage and session revocation.
sequences.invariant_hypothesis: coverage: exercise SAML login permutations and session lifecycle across two identities without asserting security invariants
